summary_for_children: Al-Qasas means The Stories. It tells how Musa's mother placed him in the river trusting Allah, how he grew up, helped two women at the well of Madyan, and was later called at the mount. It ends with Qarun, whose great wealth could not save him.
environment_concept: Reeds and calm water (28:7), the well of Madyan with flocks waiting (28:23), a tree's shade (28:24), a fire seen from the road (28:29) and a treasure house sinking into the ground (28:81).
architecture_and_scenery: A river with reeds, a palace on its bank, a desert crossing, the well of Madyan with flocks, a shady tree, a mount with fire, and a sinking treasure house.

unique_world.visual_theme: A river running down from the hills, splitting twice into channels that end in a quiet landing or a reed marsh, with palms and olives on the banks

primary_mechanic.text: Let an empty chest go at the top of the river and follow it along the bank. At each fork, move a bundle of reeds to close one channel so the chest takes the way to the quiet landing, and nudge it free where it catches on the bank. A wrong channel ends in a reed marsh and the chest is brought back to try again. Nobody rides in the chest; Musa, his mother and his sister are not shown, and the story is read (28:7, 28:11-13).

unique_world.narrative_structure: The promise to Musa's mother, the chest on the river, then two readings
world_assets: branching river with two reed gates
environment_behaviour: the chest floats with the current and bobs on the water
reed bundles visibly close the channel they block
the chest stops at snags until nudged
unique_world.learning_objective: Learn how Allah kept His promise to Musa's mother (28:7, 28:13), and the lessons of Madyan and Qarun

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: Musa's Journey and Qarun
story_library.children_narration: Musa was born during a dangerous time, but Allah protected him. His mother placed him in a chest on the river, and he was eventually returned to her. As Musa grew older, he traveled to Madyan and later received his prophetic mission. The surah also tells of Qarun, whose great wealth made him proud.

world_idea.title: The River, the Well, and the Treasure
world_idea.description: Follow the chest's path along a river, explore Madyan's water source, and examine a symbolic wealth-and-gratitude challenge connected to Qarun's story.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: Musa and his mother are not shown. The chest floats empty in the game, labelled as an adaptation. The killing in 28:15 is reading only. Qarun's fate (28:81) is narrated only.
